clips.caption: Host introduces the event and welcomes attendees, setting the stage for a packed day of talks.
Host introduces Esteban, a former Antler cohort member and current engineering lead, highlighting his expertise in AI and cloud infrastructure.
Esteban outlines the focus of his talk: evolving AI agent harnesses using reinforcement learning principles and practical engineering.
Esteban defines harnesses as the runtime components that enhance agent performance beyond basic prompts, including memory, skills, and tool management.
Esteban emphasizes that designing domain-specific benchmarks is crucial for measuring and improving agent performance over time.
Esteban discusses the gap between demo-ready and production-ready AI agents, stressing the need for tailored harnesses.
Esteban explains the value of closed-loop systems using tracing tools like Langfuse to monitor agent behavior and guide improvements.
Esteban maps RL concepts—state, action, policy, reward, update—to agent harness engineering, showing how each can be tuned.
Esteban shares results from a workshop using QIN models, showing how adding tools and skills improved performance on benchmarks.
Esteban details how to design effective benchmarks with multiple dimensions and gradients to measure agent progress accurately.
Esteban addresses the inherent unpredictability of AI agents and stresses the need for rigorous, repeatable testing to build trust.
Esteban illustrates the need for customizing agents for specific domains, using healthcare SOAP notes as a case study.
Esteban argues that runtime-injected skills provide the highest leverage for improving agent performance in real-world use cases.
Esteban explains the need for a smarter, more capable agent to judge and evolve the task agent, using Claude as a verifier.
Esteban highlights the importance of tracking performance gradients and rich artifacts like cost, pass rate, and trace details over time.
Esteban contrasts research frameworks like HarnessX with production-ready tools, advocating for custom or highly configurable harnesses.
Esteban evaluates open-source harnesses like DeepAgents.js and Cloud Code SDK, emphasizing flexibility and testability.
Esteban reflects on viewing AI systems as workflows with agentic elements, blending deterministic steps with intelligent decision-making.
Esteban shares how he used sandboxing and dynamic code generation to handle messy, variable data in a healthcare use case.
Esteban discusses how agentic behavior is essential when dealing with unpredictable inputs, such as patient symptoms or unstructured data.
Esteban proposes using code generation quality as a benchmark, ensuring agents write correct, reliable code for data processing.
Esteban recommends reading white papers, using tools like ChatGPT to simplify complex concepts, and leveraging well-documented harnesses.
Esteban advises business leaders to prioritize benchmarking and measurable progress to gain confidence in AI agent deployment.
Esteban concludes with a call to move beyond intuition and embrace data-driven evaluation of AI agents, followed by audience questions.
